transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~37 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Aurora Head of Clinical AI), Ben Ortiz (Aurora Platform), Priya Singh (Aurora Regulatory), Alex (Aurora Data Sci)

Auto-summary (auto gen - may be imperfect):
- Quick run through of weekly metrics, flags on recent regression on prompt-set B-3, discussion of guardrail tuning and scoring thresholds.

Topics: quality evaluation, regression checks, prompt A/B/C, scoring, guardrails, infra tradeoffs

[00:00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I see we have most folks — Maya, Priya, Ben, Alex — and Diego from our SE team. Quick agenda: go over the latest quality report you got this morning, dig into the B-3 regression, talk guardrail behavior, then agree next steps.
[00:00:23] Maya: Yep, thanks Samira. We have about 30 minutes but we can go longer if needed. Our main worry is the uptick in hallucinations for clinical summarization prompts — especially the ones in the post-op notes set.
[00:00:38] Ben: We also want to verify the latency on Aurora infra when we hit a 1.2k token window. That affects whether we go dedicated or keep hosted.
[00:00:50] Diego: quick note — the regressions look localized to prompt-set B3, I can share the runbook. I suspect it's prompt phrasing that exposed a model change in generation steering.
[00:01:05] Priya: From a compliance angle we need any changes to retention or logs documented — also if guardrails are blocking content that clinicians rely on, we need a clear override workflow.
[00:01:20] Samira: Understood. We'll map the guardrail decisions. Diego, can you start by walking through the scoring deltas?
[00:01:31] Diego: Sure. I'll pull up the delta table — apologies if some column headers are off in the sheet (the auto export mangled a couple names). So we compared baseline model v1.4 to today's hosted variant v1.4-patch3. Prompt set A (triage questions) was stable, prompt C (patient education) improved slightly, but B3 (post-op summaries) shows a 12% increase in hallucination rate by our metric.
[00:02:02] Alex: Can you remind us how hallucination is scored here? I thought we threshold on factual mismatch plus clinician flag.
[00:02:10] Diego: Right — our scoring rubric is combined: automated entity mismatch (NER-based) plus manual spot-checking. The sheet shows both numbers; the automated jump is 9% and the manual flagged jump is 12%. So both signal.
[00:02:26] Maya: Any idea which tokens or prefixes trigger it? We saw weird insertions like medication names that don't exist in records.
[00:02:36] Diego: There's a clear cluster in prompts that include the phrase "post-op narrative:" followed by freeform notes. The KV cache/prefix behavior on the patched runtime seems to be returning some stale cached completions for certain templates — could be batching or the cache keying.
[00:02:55] Samira: That's interesting — it could be a runtime regression rather than model weights. Diego, could you triage whether it's prefix caching versus model steer?
[00:03:05] Diego: I'll run an isolated deterministic run with caching disabled and compare. If the hallucinations disappear, it's runtime. If not, we'll look at prompt steering differences.
[00:03:18] Ben: Also, cost checks — the patched build increased tokenization overhead by about 2% in our infra runs, which could push us over budget if we keep it. We need bench tests in Aurora infra to know exact per-token cost.
[00:03:33] Priya: Quick regulatory question — if we disable caching for these cases, does that affect PII exposure or logs? We need to capture any policy implications.
[00:03:44] Diego: Disabling prefix cache will increase per-request raw compute and we might preserve fewer intermediate KV entries, but logs are unaffected; however, we can adjust retention. Samira, is there a documented recommendation for KMS key use for caches? I remember a doc but not sure it's been shared.
[00:03:59] Samira: I will re-share our security brief. There's also a link to the SOC2 artifact bundle — I'll send it after this call.
[00:04:10] Maya: Good. Back to scoring, did you run A/B on prompt variants? Alex, we also pushed a new prompt engineering attempt last week (B3-alt1).
[00:04:20] Alex: Yes — B3-alt1 reduced hallucination in synthetic tests but on live data it still had edge cases. The alt used more explicit "Do not invent medication names" instruction, but we saw the model sometimes paraphrase instead.
[00:04:35] Samira: That's a classic safety vs utility trade-off. We should document which prompts lose too much helpfulness when tightened.
[00:04:44] Diego: For today's plan I suggest three tracks: 1) regression triage (runtime vs model), 2) prompt bundle AB test with stricter constraint variants, 3) guardrail policy tuning (thresholds for auto-block vs soft-warning). Run numbers: I'll run regression jobs across the latest 4k samples and surface raw logs.
[00:05:05] Ben: For the bench test, can we do a 1-hour focused run on our dedicated instance to get latency p95 and cost estimates? We can provision spot GPUs for that.
[00:05:16] Samira: Yes, we can schedule a bench test. Diego — if you prepare the regression job specs, Samira will coordinate scheduling with Aurora infra.
[00:05:27] Diego: Got it.
[00:05:31] [00:05:31] Maya: A couple items we noticed in the report — the false positives where guardrails triggered on clinician shorthand (e.g., 's/p' for switch patient) which actually are safe. We need better lexical exceptions.
[00:05:44] Diego: We can add a small lexical whitelist for clinician shorthand to the safety filter. It's a quick fix but we should be careful not to open loopholes.
[00:05:52] Priya: Also, how are we storing the flagged items? Are we keeping raw prompts or only hashes? For compliance, we may need to keep redacteds.
[00:06:02] Samira: We can share options: full logs in a customer VPC, redacted transcripts in the dashboard, or hashed-only with retrieval workflows. I will attach the options in the follow-up.
[00:06:13] Alex: When you run the regression, Diego, can you include the prompt-indexed examples that actually changed outcome? That helps our clinical team triage.
[00:06:22] Diego: Yes, I'll include diffs per prompt id and highlight where the top-k completions changed.
[00:06:29] [00:06:29] Ben: On dedicated vs hosted — if bench tests show p95 < 250ms for our 1.2k token window on hosted, we can likely stick with hosted for now; otherwise we need a dedicated pool or burst config.
[00:06:44] Samira: Makes sense. We'll aim to measure both hosted and dedicated runs.
[00:06:50] Maya: Another observation: guardrail soft-warnings are not surfaced well in the clinician UI; they only see the blocked output. We prefer soft-warning mode with an override button and a provenance note.
[00:07:04] Samira: Noted. UX change request — I'll put that in the ticket but for the POC we can simulate via a flag to keep outputs but mark them.
[00:07:13] Diego: Quick technical aside — the runtime patch included a change to attention kernel scheduling. That could cause subtle differences in sampling for long sequences. If that maps to the B3 cases, we should run a deterministic sample with exact seed to see if sampling drift explains it.
[00:07:31] Alex: Can we get the exact seed used in the hosted runs?
[00:07:35] Diego: The hosted service uses a per-request RNG unless you pin a seed. I can force-seed for regression runs.
[00:07:43] Priya: If we pin seeds for testing, ensure we note that deterministic behavior is only for test; production stochasticity remains.
[00:07:52] Samira: Agreed.
[00:07:56] [00:07:56] Maya: On scoring: Alex and I reviewed the false negative examples — some were classified safe by the model but clinicians marked them as missing critical follow-up. We should consider adding a completeness metric, not just hallucination.
[00:08:12] Alex: I can add a completeness column to the scoring sheet and we can try a weighted score: 0.6 hallucination penalty, 0.4 completeness gap.
[00:08:21] Samira: That would be helpful. Please add a short note on how we compute completeness.
[00:08:26] Alex: Will do.
[00:08:29] [00:08:29] Ben: Any blockers on our side to run Aurora infra bench? We can spin up a test cluster Thursday.
[00:08:38] Maya: Thursday works. We need Diego's job spec by Wednesday to load the proper input set.
[00:08:44] Samira: OK Wednesday for job spec, Thursday bench.
[00:08:48] Diego: I'll prepare the spec and a config file with caching on/off permutations and batch sizes 8/16/32.
[00:08:58] Priya: Regarding guardrails and audit — we need a matrix of what triggers an auto-block versus a soft-warning, and whether the ticketing flow will be created.
[00:09:09] Samira: We'll draft a guardrail decision matrix. Diego can propose technical thresholds; Priya/Maya provide domain thresholds.
[00:09:19] Diego: I'll model thresholds as numeric scores in the sheet so they can be tuned without code changes.
[00:09:26] [00:09:26] Maya: On prompt engineering, Alex tried a constrained rewrite that performed well for short summaries but failed when clinical notes were longer than 600 tokens. We need prompt truncation strategies and maybe chunking with a final synth step.
[00:09:40] Alex: Yes, chunk-and-summarize then synth works but increases calls and latency. We can explore a hybrid: chunk critical sections only.
[00:09:50] Ben: That's where cost tradeoffs matter. If chunk-and-synth doubles calls, hosted cost may spike.
[00:09:57] Samira: For the bench test, include a scenario for chunked pipeline too so we can compare cost & latency.
[00:10:04] Diego: Will add that.
[00:10:07] [00:10:07] Maya: A question on guardrails — we've seen a few clinician shorthand false positives. Could the NER be tuned with a clinical vocab override?
[00:10:16] Diego: Yes, we can add a custom clinical lexicon to the NER preprocessing; it should reduce false positives. It's a small deploy.
[00:10:22] Priya: Please flag any lexicon changes that widen acceptance — we need to ensure privacy.
[00:10:28] Samira: We'll document it.
[00:10:31] [00:10:31] Alex: One more thing — evaluation: can we add per-case provenance so clinicians see which sentence came from EHR vs model-generated?
[00:10:40] Diego: We can attach provenance tags at the sentence level but that'll require some work in the UI. For the POC we can include inline markers like [EHR]/[Model].
[00:10:51] Ben: That helps adoption.
[00:10:53] [00:10:53] Samira: OK let's move toward concrete asks — Diego: regression triage with caching toggle, and seed-for-deterministic test. Samira: share scoring sheet and SOC2 notes. Maya/Priya: list of clinician shorthand examples and regulatory artifact needs. Alex: add completeness metric. Ben: schedule bench on Thursday and provision cluster.
[00:11:18] Diego: I'll queue the regression across 4k samples; estimate 4 hours runtime on our side, will post results and raw logs.
[00:11:27] Alex: I'll update sheet and add completeness.
[00:11:31] [00:11:31] (Brief silence/background typing)
[00:12:00] Maya: a quick thing — we saw a spike in a single case where the generated output asserted a non-existent allergy. That one is priority.
[00:12:09] Diego: If you can share the prompt id offline, I'll prioritize reproducing it.
[00:12:14] Maya: I'll paste it in the thread.
[00:12:18] Samira: Great — also for the SOC2 artifacts, Priya, we'll need to know who on your infra team will receive the docs.
[00:12:25] Priya: I'll send a distribution list after.
[00:12:29] [00:12:29] Ben: On the topic of dedicated capacity, a question: does Redwood support burst into dedicated and fall back to hosted? We've discussed fallback but need details.
[00:12:39] Samira: Yes, we support smart routing and fallbacks — we can set policy to use dedicated primarily, and if capacity exhausted, route to hosted compatible model variant with graceful degradation.
[00:12:51] Ben: Are there any version constraints across models with fallback?
[00:12:55] Diego: Fallbacks must be to a compatible family (e.g., same tokenizer, similar instruction tuning). We can define a fallback mapping per model.
[00:13:05] [00:13:05] Maya: For this week, we really need the regression results and the scoring spreadsheet — those will inform whether to tighten guardrails.
[00:13:13] Samira: Understood. We'll prioritize those.
[00:13:15] Diego: Also, I'll run a run with caching disabled, and one with cache TTL reduced to 30s to see if stale completions drop.
[00:13:25] Priya: If cache TTL is decreased, does that increase cost?
[00:13:28] Diego: Slightly yes. More cache misses means more compute. We'll quantify in the bench.
[00:13:34] [00:13:34] Alex: When you run A/B tests, include the per-prompt length distribution. Some failures cluster at >800 tokens.
[00:13:43] Diego: Noted.
[00:13:45] Samira: Anything else from Aurora side?
[00:13:49] Maya: not right now.
[00:13:51] Priya: I'll prepare the artifact list.
[00:13:54] Ben: I'll schedule the bench Thursday and share calendar invite.
[00:13:59] [00:13:59] Samira: Great. Recap of next steps in case items get lost: share sheet (Samira), regression runs (Diego), bench scheduling (Ben), completeness metric (Alex), artifact list (Priya), shorthand examples (Maya).
[00:14:16] Diego: I'll also surface raw completions so you can see exact hallucination text.
[00:14:20] Alex: Please include top-5 completions for each prompt id.
[00:14:25] Maya: That will help triage.
[00:14:27] [00:14:27] (brief cross talk - some overlap)
[00:15:00] Samira: Any questions about pricing? We got a note that the patch increases compute by ~2% in token overhead; depending on your usage profile, that could translate to small cost delta. We can model cost in the bench.
[00:15:14] Ben: We'll include cost modeling.
[00:15:18] Priya: For contractual stuff — if we need to change retention or logging, we'll need a short amendment; I'll outline that with legal.
[00:15:27] Samira: Ok.
[00:15:31] [00:15:31] (silence, attendees note-taking)
[00:16:00] Diego: One more technical note: we identified a minor mismatch in tokenizer handling for certain unicode characters (emdash vs hyphen) that can change token counts. That could explain some p95 variance. I'll normalize during regression.
[00:16:14] Alex: Good catch.
[00:16:16] Maya: Anything else?
[00:16:18] Ben: No.
[00:16:20] [00:16:20] Samira: Alright everyone — thanks for the quick, focused sync. We'll reconvene next week unless we need a mid-week checkpoint after regression results.
[00:16:30] Priya: mid-week sounds good if there are high-priority findings.
[00:16:34] Samira: I'll send the notes and action items after this.
[00:16:38] (meeting wraps, some people drop)

Post-call notes (auto):
- Triaged likely runtime vs model regression; Diego to run controlled regression with caching toggles and seeded runs.
- Scoring sheet to be updated with completeness metric.
- Bench test scheduled tentatively for Thursday on Aurora infra to measure p95 and cost on chunked vs single-run pipeline.
- Guardrail tuning plan: numeric thresholds to be editable; add clinical lexicon exceptions.

References / links mentioned (to be shared in follow-up):
- scoring spreadsheet (link to be posted)
- SOC2 / security brief (Samira will attach)
- bench run spec (Diego to post)

End transcript.
